complete.problem: Build sodium chloride step by step.
complete.selfExplanation: Explain how the electron transfer forms the two ions, and how the lattice gives the 1 to 1 ratio behind the formula NaCl.

steps.annotation: The attraction between oppositely charged ions, formed when one atom transfers outer electrons to another.
steps.text: Step 1 (s1): sodium (2,8,1) has one outer electron and chlorine (2,8,7) needs one, so the electron transfers: sodium forms a positive sodium ion with arrangement 2,8 and chlorine forms a negative chloride ion with arrangement 2,8,8.

steps.annotation: A giant regular repeating pattern of particles. In an ionic compound every ion is surrounded by oppositely charged ions, with no separate molecules.
steps.text: Step 2 (s2): the ions attract each other in every direction and lock into a giant lattice where the ions alternate, so the ratio is one sodium to one chloride and the formula is NaCl.

steps.annotation: A charged particle formed when an atom loses electrons (positive ion) or gains electrons (negative ion).
steps.text: Check the count: every sodium ion is surrounded by chloride ions and the pattern never breaks into pairs - that is the sign of a lattice, not molecules.

faded.problem: Magnesium has electron arrangement 2,8,2 and oxygen has 2,6. State the ions formed when they bond, and the type of bond.
faded.selfExplanation: The first step is shown. Say how the two outer electrons move, then name the ions and the bond type.

steps.annotation: A charged particle formed when an atom loses electrons (positive ion) or gains electrons (negative ion).
steps.text: Step 1: magnesium has electron arrangement 2,8,2, so it has 2 outer electrons to lose.

steps.annotation: A strong answer moves the electrons first, then names the ions: losing electrons makes a positive ion, gaining makes a negative one. If you wrote that the atoms share electrons, that describes covalent bonding instead.
steps.text: Step 2: magnesium loses its 2 outer electrons to form a positive magnesium ion, and oxygen gains 2 electrons to form a negative oxide ion.

steps.annotation: The slip: The formula NaCl looks like one joined unit, like the formulas of real molecules. The fix: Salt is a giant ionic lattice: NaCl just gives the ratio, there are no separate NaCl molecules. In class, draw one corner of the lattice and ask students to circle a single NaCl molecule - they cannot, because each ion belongs to the whole pattern, not to one partner.
steps.text: Step 3: the oppositely charged ions attract each other, so the bond is ionic.

paired.problem: A chlorine molecule, Cl2, is held together by a covalent bond. Explain, in terms of electrons, how the bond forms and why no ions are made.
paired.solution: Each chlorine atom contributes one electron to a shared pair between the two atoms. Both atoms count the shared pair in their outer shell, so each has eight outer electrons. No electron is transferred, so no ions form.
